```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(ezRun)
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(DT)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggrepel)

.fgcz_load <- function(name, nthreads = 4L) {
  for (p in c(paste0(name, ".qs2"), paste0(name, ".rds"))) {
    if (file.exists(p)) {
      if (grepl("\\.qs2$", p)) {
        return(qs2::qs_read(p, nthreads = nthreads))
      }
      return(readRDS(p))
    }
  }
  NULL
}
param <- .fgcz_load("param")
results <- .fgcz_load("results")
scData <- .fgcz_load("scData")
scData.unfiltered <- .fgcz_load("scData.unfiltered")
sampleName <- results$sampleName
DefaultAssay(scData) <- "SCT"

.ok <- function(step) {
  isTRUE(results$status[[step]]$ok)
}
.status_callout <- function(step) {
  st <- results$status[[step]]
  if (is.null(st) || isTRUE(st$ok)) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  if (is.na(st$ok)) {
    cat(sprintf("::: {.callout-note}\nThis step was skipped: %s.\n:::\n", st$msg))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(
      "::: {.callout-warning}\nThis step failed and is not shown: `%s`\n:::\n",
      gsub("`", "'", st$msg)
    ))
  }
}
.dt <- function(df, pageLength = 10L, digits = 3) {
  num <- vapply(df, is.numeric, TRUE)
  df[num] <- lapply(df[num], signif, digits = digits)
  DT::datatable(
    df,
    rownames = FALSE,
    filter = "top",
    extensions = "Buttons",
    options = list(
      pageLength = pageLength,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      dom = "Bfrtip",
      buttons = c("copy", "csv", "excel")
    )
  )
}

## Colour-blind safe categorical palette: Okabe-Ito, then Paul Tol muted and
## light. Spatial maps also carry direct labels, so colour is never the only
## cue.
.cat_pal <- function(levels) {
  base <- c(
    "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00",
    "#CC79A7", "#999999", "#332288", "#88CCEE", "#44AA99", "#117733",
    "#DDCC77", "#CC6677", "#AA4499", "#882255", "#77AADD", "#EE8866",
    "#BBCC33", "#AAAA00", "#FFAABB", "#000000"
  )
  n <- length(levels)
  cols <- if (n <= length(base)) {
    base[seq_len(n)]
  } else {
    grDevices::hcl.colors(n, "Dark 3")
  }
  stats::setNames(cols, levels)
}

## Spot coordinates in image orientation (no histology); fast for small
## multiples.
spots <- data.frame(
  x = scData$pxl_col_fullres,
  y = -scData$pxl_row_fullres,
  scData[[]],
  check.names = FALSE
)
.spot_size <- 1.1
.spot_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(aspect.ratio = diff(range(spots$y)) / diff(range(spots$x)))
.label_centroids <- function(df, group) {
  df %>%
    group_by(.data[[group]]) %>%
    summarise(x = median(x), y = median(y), .groups = "drop")
}
.spot_discrete <- function(df, group, title = group, labels = TRUE) {
  lev <- levels(factor(df[[group]]))
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x, y, colour = .data[[group]])) +
    geom_point(size = .spot_size, shape = 16) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = .cat_pal(lev), name = NULL) +
    labs(title = title) +
    .spot_theme +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))
  if (labels) {
    p <- p + geom_label_repel(
      data = .label_centroids(df, group),
      aes(label = .data[[group]]),
      colour = "black",
      fill = alpha("white", 0.8),
      size = 2.8,
      label.size = 0.1,
      min.segment.length = 0,
      seed = 1
    )
  }
  p
}
.spot_continuous <- function(df, value, title = value, option = "viridis", limits = NULL) {
  v <- df[[value]]
  if (is.null(limits)) {
    limits <- stats::quantile(v, c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  df$.v <- pmin(pmax(v, limits[1]), limits[2])
  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, colour = .v)) +
    geom_point(size = .spot_size, shape = 16) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = option, name = NULL) +
    labs(title = title) +
    .spot_theme
}
.feature_df <- function(features, assay = "SCT") {
  m <- FetchData(scData, vars = features, layer = "data")
  cbind(spots[, c("x", "y")], m)
}
.spot_feature_grid <- function(features, assay = "SCT", ncol = 4, option = "viridis") {
  features <- unique(features)
  DefaultAssay(scData) <- assay
  df <- .feature_df(features, assay)
  plots <- lapply(features, function(f) .spot_continuous(df, f, title = f, option = option))
  wrap_plots(plots, ncol = ncol)
}
## a heading that only appears when its step was not skipped (optional
## add-ons that are off by default would otherwise leave empty tabs)
.step_heading <- function(step, heading, level = 1) {
  st <- results$status[[step]]
  if (!is.null(st) && !is.na(st$ok)) {
    cat(strrep("#", level), " ", heading, "\n\n", sep = "")
    .status_callout(step)
  }
}
deconMethod <- if (identical(results$rctd$engine, "CARD")) "CARD" else "RCTD"
dominantCol <- results$rctd$dominantCol %||% "rctd_dominant"
domainCol <- if ("domain_label" %in% colnames(spots)) "domain_label" else "banksy_domain"
nDomains <- nlevels(factor(spots$banksy_domain))
nClusters <- nlevels(factor(spots$expr_cluster))
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

# Overview

::: {.callout-note title="What this report is"}
A per-sample analysis of one Visium SD section (55 µm spots, each covering
roughly 1-10 cells). The analysis goes from spot quality control over
expression clusters to **spatial domains** (BANKSY), their anatomical
annotation, spatially variable genes, cell-type deconvolution, domain
neighbourhoods, pathway and transcription-factor activities, spatial
dependencies between cell types (MISTy) and a distance-constrained
ligand-receptor analysis. Every tab starts with a short
explanation of what was computed and how to read the plots. The objects behind
the report are described in the tab *Data & explore in R*.
:::

```{r overview-image}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| out-width: "55%"
#| fig-cap: "The tissue section (hires image) with the spots that passed QC."
SpatialDimPlot(scData, group.by = "Sample", alpha = c(0.25, 0.25),
               pt.size.factor = param$pt.size.factor, cols = "#0072B2") +
  NoLegend()
```

```{r overview-table}
keyNumbers <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Quantity, ~Value,
  "Spots on the capture area", format(results$spotInfo$nSpotsTotal, big.mark = ","),
  "Spots under tissue", format(qi$nSpotsTissue, big.mark = ","),
  "Spots kept after QC", format(qi$nSpotsKept, big.mark = ","),
  "Genes kept", format(qi$nGenesKept, big.mark = ","),
  "Median UMIs per spot", format(median(scData$nCount_Spatial), big.mark = ","),
  "Median genes per spot", format(median(scData$nFeature_Spatial), big.mark = ","),
  "Chemistry", if (isTRUE(qi$probeBased)) "probe-based (FFPE / CytAssist)" else "poly-A capture",
  "Expression clusters", as.character(nClusters),
```

# Quality control

::: {.callout-note title="What and why"}
A spot is not a cell: its UMI and gene counts reflect both quality **and**
anatomy. Fiber tracts and white matter contain few, RNA-poor cells and
therefore have few UMIs, while dense neuronal layers have many. A single
global threshold would remove whole anatomical structures. Spots are
therefore flagged with **SpotSweeper** as *local* outliers: a spot is only
removed if it has far fewer UMIs/genes than its 36 nearest spatial
neighbours.
:::

```{r qc-mito-note}
#| results: asis
if (!isTRUE(results$qcInfo$useMito)) {
  cat("::: {.callout-important title=\"No mitochondrial genes\"}\n",
      "The data come from a probe-based chemistry (FFPE / CytAssist). The probe panel ",
      "contains no mitochondrial genes, so the mitochondrial fraction is zero in every ",
      "spot and is not used for QC.\n:::\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r qc-maps}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-cap: "UMIs and genes per spot before filtering (log10), and the spots removed by QC (red-free highlight: removed spots are black)."
unf <- data.frame(
  x = scData.unfiltered$pxl_col_fullres,
  y = -scData.unfiltered$pxl_row_fullres,
  logUMI = log10(scData.unfiltered$nCount_Spatial + 1),
  logGenes = log10(scData.unfiltered$nFeature_Spatial + 1),
  removed = factor(ifelse(scData.unfiltered$discard, "removed", "kept"), levels = c("kept", "removed"))
)
(.spot_continuous(unf, "logUMI", "log10 UMIs") |
  .spot_continuous(unf, "logGenes", "log10 genes") |
  ggplot(unf, aes(x, y, colour = removed)) +
    geom_point(size = .spot_size, shape = 16) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(kept = "#BBBBBB", removed = "#000000"), name = NULL) +
    labs(title = "QC result") + .spot_theme)
```

```{r qc-table}
flags <- results$qcInfo$flags
kable(tibble(
  Flag = c("Low UMIs (local outlier)", "Low genes (local outlier)",
           "High mitochondrial fraction", "High ribosomal fraction"),
  Spots = as.integer(flags)
)) %>% kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
```

```{r qc-violin}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| out-width: "70%"
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of UMIs and genes per spot; removed spots in black."
data.frame(
  UMIs = scData.unfiltered$nCount_Spatial,
  Genes = scData.unfiltered$nFeature_Spatial,
  removed = unf$removed
) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(UMIs, Genes)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(name, value)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "#56B4E9", colour = NA, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = removed), width = 0.2, size = 0.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(kept = "#888888", removed = "#000000")) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Normalisation

::: {.callout-note title="What and why"}
Counts are normalised with **SCTransform** (regularised negative binomial
regression on the UMI count of each spot). Library size in spatial data is
partly biological: the plots show UMIs per spot by expression cluster.
Normalisation removes this depth effect for clustering, but the raw UMI map
in the QC tab remains an anatomical readout in itself.
:::

```{r norm-depth}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| out-width: "90%"
p1 <- ggplot(spots, aes(expr_cluster, nCount_Spatial, fill = expr_cluster)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = .cat_pal(levels(factor(spots$expr_cluster)))) +
  labs(x = "Expression cluster", y = "UMIs per spot") +
  theme_bw() + NoLegend()
p2 <- ElbowPlot(scData, ndims = 50) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(param$npcs), linetype = 2) +
  labs(title = sprintf("PCs used: %s", param$npcs)) + theme_bw()
p1 | p2
```

# Expression clusters

::: {.callout-note title="What and why"}
Spots are clustered on their own expression only (PCA, nearest-neighbour graph,
Louvain, resolution `r param$resolution`). The spatial position is **not**
used. Compare the spatial map with the BANKSY domains in the next tab:
expression clusters are often patchy, because neighbouring spots mix different
cell types.
:::

```{r expr-maps}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| out-width: "100%"
umapDf <- data.frame(Embeddings(scData, "umap"), cluster = scData$expr_cluster)
colnames(umapDf)[1:2] <- c("UMAP_1", "UMAP_2")
pu <- ggplot(umapDf, aes(UMAP_1, UMAP_2, colour = cluster)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  geom_label_repel(data = umapDf %>% group_by(cluster) %>%
                     summarise(UMAP_1 = median(UMAP_1), UMAP_2 = median(UMAP_2)),
                   aes(label = cluster), colour = "black", size = 3, seed = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = .cat_pal(levels(umapDf$cluster))) +
  theme_classic() + NoLegend()
pu | .spot_discrete(spots, "expr_cluster", "Expression clusters on the section")
```

```{r expr-clustree}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "60%"
#| fig-cap: "Cluster tree across resolutions: stable clusters keep their spots when the resolution increases."
tryCatch(
  print(clustree::clustree(scData, prefix = "SCT_snn_res.")),
  error = function(e) {
    ## clustree/ggraph versions are not always compatible with ggplot2
    tab <- as.data.frame(lapply(scData[[grep("^SCT_snn_res", colnames(scData[[]]), value = TRUE)]], nlevels))
    print(ggplot(tibble(resolution = as.numeric(sub("SCT_snn_res.", "", names(tab))), clusters = unlist(tab)),
                 aes(resolution, clusters)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + theme_bw() +
            labs(title = "Number of clusters per resolution"))
  }
)
```

# BANKSY domains

::: {.callout-note title="What and why"}
**BANKSY** (Singhal et al., *Nat Genet* 2024) augments every spot's expression
with the average expression of its `r param$banksyKgeom` nearest neighbours.
The parameter **λ** sets the weight of the neighbourhood: λ = 0 is plain
expression clustering, λ ≈ 0.2 helps cell typing, and λ = 0.8 (used here)
segments the tissue into contiguous **spatial domains**. In the brain these
correspond to layers, nuclei and fiber tracts.

How to read: the λ panels show the same clustering with increasing spatial
weight. *Smoothness* is the fraction of a spot's direct neighbours that carry
the same label (1 = perfectly contiguous); the *ARI* measures how similar the
partition is to the expression clusters (1 = identical).
:::

```{r banksy-sweep}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "100%"
sweepCols <- paste0("banksy_lambda_", results$banksySweep$lambda)
plots <- lapply(seq_along(sweepCols), function(i) {
  s <- results$banksySweep[i, ]
  .spot_discrete(spots, sweepCols[i], labels = FALSE,
                 title = sprintf("λ = %s: %d domains, smoothness %.2f",
                                 s$lambda, s$nDomains, s$smoothness)) +
    NoLegend()
})
wrap_plots(plots, nrow = 1)
```

```{r banksy-sweep-table}
kable(results$banksySweep, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("λ", "Domains", "Smoothness", "ARI vs expression clusters")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
```

# Domain annotation

```{r anno-status}
#| results: asis
.status_callout("domainAnnotation")
```

```{r anno-intro}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr .ok("domainAnnotation")
cat("::: {.callout-note title=\"What and why\"}\n",
    "Every spot is scored (UCell) for curated marker sets of anatomical regions ",
    "(cortical layers, hippocampal fields, striatum, thalamus, amygdala, piriform cortex, fiber tracts, ",
    "ventricles, meninges ...). The scores are z-scaled and averaged per domain; a ",
    "domain gets the name of its best region if it beats the second best by a ",
    "margin, otherwise it is called *mixed*. The labels are a starting point for ",
    "interpretation, not ground truth: check them against the histology, the domain ",
    "markers and the deconvolution.\n:::\n", sep = "")
```

```{r anno-heatmap}

lab <- results$domainAnno$domainLabels
rownames(sc) <- lab$domain_label[match(rownames(sc), lab$domain)]
as.data.frame(as.table(sc)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Var2, Var1, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", name = "z") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Spatially variable genes

```{r svg-status}
#| results: asis
.status_callout("spatiallyVariableGenes")
```

```{r svg-intro}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr .ok("spatiallyVariableGenes")
cat("::: {.callout-note title=\"What and why\"}\n",
    "A spatially variable gene (SVG) has an expression pattern that is ",
    "**autocorrelated in space**: neighbouring spots have similar values. ",
    "**Moran's I** (here on the hexagonal grid of direct spot neighbours) is about ",
    "0 for random patterns and approaches 1 for smooth gradients or large ",
    "contiguous regions. The top genes are additionally ranked with **nnSVG** ",
    "(Weber et al., *Nat Commun* 2023), a Gaussian-process model whose `prop_sv` is ",
    "the fraction of variance that is spatial. SVGs are not the same as cluster ",
    "markers: an SVG needs no predefined groups and can follow gradients that cut ",
    "across domains. The top SVGs are grouped into spatial **patterns** ",
    "(hierarchical clustering of their smoothed profiles).\n:::\n", sep = "")
```


# Deconvolution

```{r rctd-status}
#| results: asis
.status_callout("deconvolution")
```

```{r rctd-intro}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr .ok("deconvolution")
method <- if (deconMethod == "CARD") {
  paste0("**CARD** (Ma & Zhou, *Nat Biotechnol* 2022) models each spot's counts as a ",
         "mixture of reference cell-type profiles and lets neighbouring spots share ",
         "information (a spatial prior), so proportions vary smoothly across the tissue")
} else {
  paste0("**RCTD** (Cable et al., *Nat Biotechnol* 2022; run with ",
         results$rctd$engine %||% "spacexr", ") models each spot's counts as a mixture ",
         "of reference cell-type profiles and estimates the **proportion** of every ",
         "type (full mode)")
}
cat("::: {.callout-note title=\"What and why\"}\n",
    "A Visium spot contains several cells. ", method, ". The reference is `",
    results$rctd$reference, "`. Proportions are estimates: rare types and types ",
    "missing from the reference cannot be recovered, and similar types can trade ",
    "weight with each other.\n:::\n", sep = "")
```

```{r rctd-maps}
#| eval: !expr .ok("deconvolution")
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 10
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-cap: "Estimated proportion of the 16 most abundant cell types."
w <- results$rctd$weights
topTypes <- names(sort(colMeans(w, na.rm = TRUE), decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(16, ncol(w)))]
wdf <- cbind(spots[rownames(w), c("x", "y")], w[, topTypes, drop = FALSE])
plots <- lapply(topTypes, function(ct) {
  .spot_continuous(wdf, ct, title = ct, option = "rocket", limits = c(0, max(0.05, quantile(wdf[[ct]], 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))))
})
wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 4)
```

```{r rctd-dominant}
#| eval: !expr .ok("deconvolution")
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| out-width: "80%"
#| fig-cap: "Cell type with the highest proportion per spot."
.spot_discrete(spots, dominantCol, "Dominant cell type")
```

```{r rctd-composition}
#| eval: !expr .ok("deconvolution")
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: !expr max(4, 0.35 * nDomains + 2)
#| out-width: "90%"
#| fig-cap: "Mean cell-type composition of every domain; types below 3% everywhere are pooled."
comp <- results$rctd$composition
long <- comp %>% pivot_longer(-domain, names_to = "cell_type", values_to = "proportion")
keepTypes <- long %>% group_by(cell_type) %>% summarise(m = max(proportion)) %>% filter(m >= 0.03) %>% pull(cell_type)
long <- long %>% mutate(cell_type = ifelse(cell_type %in% keepTypes, cell_type, "other")) %>%
  group_by(domain, cell_type) %>% summarise(proportion = sum(proportion), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(long, aes(proportion, domain, fill = cell_type)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = .cat_pal(sort(unique(long$cell_type))), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "mean proportion", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Neighbourhoods

```{r nb-status}
#| results: asis
.status_callout("neighbourhood")
```

```{r nb-intro}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr .ok("neighbourhood")
cat("::: {.callout-note title=\"What and why\"}\n",
    "**Domain adjacency**: the number of spot-to-spot contacts between two domains is ",
    "compared with random relabelling of the spots (z-score). Positive values mean ",
    "the domains border each other, e.g. consecutive cortical layers; the diagonal ",
    "measures how compact a domain is.\n\n",
    "**Cell-type co-localisation**: correlation of the cell-type proportions across spots ",
    "(*same spot*) and between a spot and the mean of its neighbours (*neighbourhood*). ",
    "Positive values mean two cell types occur together.\n:::\n", sep = "")
```

```{r nb-adjacency}
#| eval: !expr .ok("neighbourhood")
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| out-width: "70%"
z <- results$neighbourhood$domainAdjacency$zScore
hc <- hclust(dist(z))
z <- z[hc$order, hc$order]
as.data.frame(as.table(z)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Var1, Var2, fill = pmax(pmin(Freq, 20), -20))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", name = "z (capped)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Domain adjacency enrichment") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r nb-coloc}
#| eval: !expr .ok("neighbourhood") && !is.null(results$neighbourhood$colocalisation)
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| out-width: "100%"
co <- results$neighbourhood$colocalisation
ord <- hclust(as.dist(1 - co$lagged))$order
plot_cor <- function(m, title) {
  m <- m[ord, ord]
  as.data.frame(as.table(m)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(Var1, Var2, fill = Freq)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(-1, 1), name = "r") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = title) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))
}
plot_cor(co$spot, "Same spot") | plot_cor(co$lagged, "Neighbourhood (spatially lagged)")
```

# Spatial dependencies

```{r misty-status}
#| results: asis
.status_callout("misty")
```

```{r misty-intro}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr .ok("misty")
mp <- results$misty$params
cat("::: {.callout-note title=\"What and why\"}\n",
    "**MISTy** (Tanevski et al., *Genome Biol* 2022) asks for every cell type how well its ",
    "proportion in a spot is predicted by three *views*: the other cell types in the same ",
    "spot (**intra**), the cell types in the directly neighbouring spots (**juxta**, within ",
    1.5 * mp$spacing, " \u00b5m) and the cell types in the wider neighbourhood (**para**, ",
    "Gaussian weights with a ", mp$paraRange, " \u00b5m length scale). One random forest is ",
    "trained per cell type (", mp$cvFolds, "-fold cross-validation).\n\n",
    "- **Gain in R\u00b2**: how much the surroundings (juxta + para) add to the prediction from ",
    "the spot itself. A high gain means the cell type sits in a typical neighbourhood.\n",
    "- **Importance**: which neighbouring cell types carry that information. It is an ",
    "association in either direction (together or apart), not a causal effect.\n\n",
    "Proportions within a spot sum to one, so the intra view is partly a bookkeeping ",
    "effect; read the juxta and para views for spatial structure.\n:::\n", sep = "")
```

```{r misty-gain}
#| eval: !expr .ok("misty")
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: !expr max(4, 0.3 * results$misty$params$nTypes + 1.5)
#| out-width: "70%"
#| fig-cap: "Variance explained per cell type: from the spot itself (intra) and with the neighbourhood views added (multi-view)."
imp <- results$misty$improvements %>%
  select(target, measure, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = value)
imp %>%
  select(target, intra = intra.R2, `multi-view` = multi.R2, gain = gain.R2) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(intra, `multi-view`), names_to = "model", values_to = "R2") %>%
  ggplot(aes(R2, reorder(target, gain), fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(intra = "#999999", `multi-view` = "#0072B2"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "variance explained (R\u00b2, %)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r misty-importance}
#| eval: !expr .ok("misty")
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: !expr max(5, 0.3 * results$misty$params$nTypes + 2.5)
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-cap: "Importance of each predictor cell type (columns) for each target (rows) in the neighbourhood views; values are scaled per target, negative values are shown as 0, grey = the cell type itself."
views <- setdiff(unique(results$misty$importances$view), "intra")
plot_imp <- function(v) {
  results$misty$importances %>%
    filter(view == v) %>%
    mutate(Importance = pmax(Importance, 0)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(Predictor, Target, fill = Importance)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, name = "importance") +
    labs(x = "predictor (around the spot)", y = "target", title = v) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))
}
wrap_plots(lapply(views, plot_imp), nrow = 1)
```

```{r misty-table}
#| eval: !expr .ok("misty")
.dt(imp %>% select(target, any_of(c("intra.R2", "multi.R2", "gain.R2", "p.R2"))) %>% arrange(desc(gain.R2)))
```

# Cell-cell communication

```{r ccc-status}
#| results: asis
.status_callout("communication")
```

```{r ccc-intro}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr .ok("communication") || .ok("spatialCellChat") || .ok("liana")
cat("::: {.callout-note title=\"What and why\"}\n",
    "**CellChat** v2 in spatial mode (Jin et al., *Nat Protoc* 2025) scores secreted ",
    "ligand-receptor pairs between groups of spots, but only between groups whose spots ",
    "lie within ", param$cellchatInteractionLength, " \u00b5m, and it down-weights distant ",
    "pairs. It is run twice: between **domains** and between the **dominant cell type** ",
    "of each spot (from the deconvolution). A spot mixes several cells, so read the ",
    "result as *which signals could be exchanged between these regions or cell types*, ",
    "a hypothesis to test with single-cell resolution data.\n:::\n", sep = "")
```

```{r ccc-helpers}
#| include: false
.ccc_heatmap <- function(pw, what) {
  agg <- pw %>% group_by(source, target) %>% summarise(prob = sum(prob), .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(agg, aes(target, source, fill = prob)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "probability") +
    labs(x = paste("receiver", what), y = paste("sender", what)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}
.ccc_top <- function(pw) {
  pw %>% group_by(pathway_name) %>% summarise(prob = sum(prob)) %>%
    slice_max(prob, n = 20) %>%
    ggplot(aes(prob, reorder(pathway_name, prob))) +
    geom_col(fill = "#0072B2") +
    labs(x = "total communication probability", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal()
}
.ccc_table <- function(lr) {
  .dt(lr[, intersect(
    c("source", "target", "ligand", "receptor", "prob", "pval", "interaction_name_2", "pathway_name"),
    colnames(lr))])
}
.has_level <- function(level) .ok("communication") && !is.null(results$communication[[level]])
```

```{r scc-intro}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr .ok("spatialCellChat")
sp <- results$spatialCellChat$params
cat("**SpatialCellChat** (CellChat v3) first scores every ligand-receptor pair between ",
    "individual neighbouring spots (secreted signals up to ", sp$interactionRange,
    " \u00b5m, contact-dependent signals only within a spot) and then averages the spot ",
    "pairs to cell types, weighted by each spot's cell-type proportions (",
    sp$nSpots, " spots, ", sp$nTypes, " cell types). Unlike the CellChat results above, ",
    "a spot contributes to every cell type it contains, not only its dominant one.\n\n", sep = "")
```

```{r bayes-intro}
    " (1 = identical). Smoothness (fraction of neighbouring spots with the same domain): ",
```

#### Load the object

```r
library(Seurat)
scData <- qs2::qs_read("scData.qs2")
SpatialDimPlot(scData, group.by = "domain_label", label = TRUE)
SpatialFeaturePlot(scData, features = "Ppp1r1b")
## cell-type proportions (assay RCTD, or CARD when CARD was chosen)
DefaultAssay(scData) <- "RCTD"
SpatialFeaturePlot(scData, features = rownames(scData)[1:4])
```

#### What is where in `scData`

```{r data-slots}
slotTab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Location, ~Content,
  "assay Spatial", "raw UMI counts",
  "assay SCT", "SCTransform-normalised expression (default assay)",
  "assay RCTD (or CARD)", "cell-type proportions (features = cell types)",
  "assays progeny / dorothea", "pathway and TF activity scores",
  "reductions pca / umap", "expression-only embedding",
  "reductions pca.banksy / umap.banksy", "BANKSY embedding",
  "graphs spatial_hex1 / spatial_hex2", "spot adjacency: direct neighbours / two rings",
  "meta.data expr_cluster", "expression clusters",
  "meta.data banksy_domain, domain_label", "BANKSY domains and their region label",
  "meta.data banksy_lambda_*", "domains of the λ sweep",
  "meta.data *_region", "UCell scores of the region marker sets",
  "meta.data svg_pattern_*", "spatial pattern scores",
  "meta.data rctd_dominant (card_dominant)", "most abundant cell type per spot",
  "meta.data bayesspace_domain", "BayesSpace domains (only when computed)",
  "meta.data array_row/array_col, pxl_*_fullres", "array and full-resolution pixel coordinates"
)
kable(slotTab) %>% kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left")
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Suggested exercises"}
1. Change λ: compare `banksy_lambda_0` and `banksy_lambda_0.8`. Which anatomical
   structures only appear with spatial information?
2. Pick a domain labelled *mixed*: look at its markers and its cell-type composition
   and give it a better name.
3. Find an SVG that is **not** a marker of any domain. What pattern does it follow?
4. Remove the QC filter: load `scData.unfiltered.qs2` and look where the removed
   spots are. Would a global UMI threshold have removed fiber tracts?
5. Compare the domains of the two replicate sections (run the same code on both).
:::

# Methods

```{r methods}
#| results: asis
.v <- function(pkg) as.character(packageVersion(pkg))
txt <- sprintf(paste0(
  "Space Ranger output was loaded with Seurat (v%s). Spots under tissue were flagged as low-quality ",
  "when they were local outliers in UMIs or detected genes compared with their 36 nearest spots ",
  "(SpotSweeper, 3 MADs%s). Genes were normalised with SCTransform v2 (%s variable genes). ",
  "Expression clusters were computed on %s principal components (Louvain, resolution %s). ",
  "Spatial domains were identified with BANKSY (\u03bb = %s, k_geom = %s, %s PCs, resolution %s) and ",
  "annotated by UCell scores of curated region marker sets. Spatially variable genes were ranked by ",
  "Moran's I on the hexagonal spot graph and the top %s by nnSVG."),
  .v("Seurat"),
  if (isTRUE(results$qcInfo$useMito)) "; and high mitochondrial fraction" else "",
  param$nfeatures, param$npcs, param$resolution,
  param$banksyLambda, param$banksyKgeom, param$banksyNpcs, param$banksyResolution,
  param$nnsvgTopN)
if (.ok("bayesspace")) {
  bp <- results$bayesspace$params
  txt <- c(txt, sprintf("For comparison, domains were also computed with BayesSpace (v%s, q = %s, %s PCs, %s iterations).",
                        bp$version, bp$q, bp$d, bp$nrep))
}
if (.ok("deconvolution")) {
  txt <- c(txt, if (deconMethod == "CARD") {
    sprintf("Cell-type proportions were estimated with CARD (v%s, reference %s, at most 300 cells per type).",
            .v("CARD"), results$rctd$reference)
  } else {
    sprintf("Cell-type proportions were estimated with RCTD (%s, full mode, reference %s).",
            if (identical(results$rctd$engine, "rctd-py")) "rctd-py" else paste0("spacexr v", .v("spacexr")),
            results$rctd$reference)
  })
}
if (.ok("activity")) {
  txt <- c(txt, "Pathway and TF activities were inferred with decoupleR (PROGENy, DoRothEA A-C).")
}
if (.ok("misty")) {
  mp <- results$misty$params
  txt <- c(txt, sprintf(paste0(
    "Spatial dependencies between cell-type proportions were modelled with MISTy (mistyR v%s; ",
    "intra, juxta (%s \u00b5m) and para (Gaussian, l = %s \u00b5m) views; random forests, %s-fold cross-validation)."),
    mp$version, 1.5 * mp$spacing, mp$paraRange, mp$cvFolds))
}
if (.ok("communication")) {
  cp <- results$communication$domain$params
  txt <- c(txt, sprintf(paste0(
    "Ligand-receptor communication between domains%s was inferred with CellChat (v%s, spatial mode, ",
    "%s \u00b5m interaction range, %s permutations, %s)."),
    if (!is.null(results$communication$celltype)) " and between the dominant cell types of the spots" else "",
    cp$version, cp$interactionRange, cp$nboot, cp$db))
}
if (.ok("spatialCellChat")) {
  sp <- results$spatialCellChat$params
  txt <- c(txt, sprintf(paste0(
    "Spot-level communication was inferred with SpatialCellChat (v%s; %s \u00b5m interaction range) and ",
    "averaged to cell types weighted by the deconvolution (%s permutations)."),
    sp$version, sp$interactionRange, sp$nboot))
}
if (.ok("liana")) {
  txt <- c(txt, sprintf(paste0(
    "Ligand-receptor pairs between touching domains were ranked with liana (v%s; NATMI, Connectome, ",
    "log2FC and SingleCellSignalR, consensus resource)."), .v("liana")))
}
cat(paste(txt, collapse = " "))
```
